dedupe_keys.name: reversible high temperature heat pumps for peak load coverage in geothermal heating plants a techno economic analysis

description: Florian Kaufmann and Christopher Schifflechner document annual simulations and techno-economic comparison of peak-load technologies for geothermal heating plants. Reversible heat-pump/ORC equipment is compared with conventional high-temperature heat pumps and gas boilers. A physical air-cooled condenser model represents part-load performance and alternative condenser sizes. The abstract reports levelised heat costs under 2024 energy prices and sensitivity to gas and electricity-price assumptions. These are model-dependent comparisons, not realised plant accounts. Zenodo supplies the paper freely under CC BY 4.0; model code access and reuse terms are unknown. Coverage is a geothermal plant configuration without a location stated in the abstract. Related FlexGeo experiments address reversible-machine behaviour. A limitation is that complete cost inputs, system boundaries and validation evidence are unavailable in the metadata inspected. No paper body was fetched and the cost results were not reproduced.
